feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: 'Genius grant' winner Immanuel Wilkins explains how he weaves Black history into his music
entry.summary: Saxophonist and composer Immanuel Wilkins talks about the impact that winning a 2026 MacArthur Fellowship will have on his art.

entry.title: For reporters covering AI, keeping up with story is both tough and exciting
entry.summary: How NPR's team covering AI covers their increasingly important and fast moving beat.

entry.title: Bayeux Tapestry's London tour spurs enthusiasts to Battle of Hastings reenactment
entry.summary: A reenactment of the Battle of Hastings, which took place almost a millennium ago, is drawing crowds of enthusiasts in the UK.

entry.title: Trump's economic strategy resemble similar policies in East Asia
entry.summary: Much of the Trump administration's economic policy has been inspired by successful industrial policies successful in East Asia, including those of competitor, China. Will those policies work in the U.S.?

entry.title: Why aren't men talking about Cornell?
entry.summary: NPR's Joel Rose speaks with culture writer Louis Staples about his piece for Harper's Bazaar titled: Women Everywhere Are Talking About Cornell. Why Aren't Men?

entry.title: What are they saying about AI at San Francisco Tech Week?
entry.summary: Tech workers gathered in San Francisco this week to talk about the opportunities they see for their industry, their mixed feelings about AI, and the high cost of living in the Bay Area.

entry.title: Isaias becomes tropical storm, heads towards Tennessee Valley
entry.summary: Isaias has become a tropical storm, moving towards the Tennessee Valley. Residents in the Florida Panhandle react to the destruction.

entry.title: Protests against voter roll revisions rock capital of world's largest democracy
entry.summary: Parts of the capital city of India, the world's largest democracy, are on lockdown. Protests over sweeping revisions to the voter rolls were met with a massive police crackdown.

entry.title: The Kennedy Center names new artistic director, amid concerns
entry.summary: The center's executive director has named an agent who has worked with ZZ Top and Motley Crue drummer Tommy Lee as the head of programming for the arts institution.

entry.title: South African human rights lawyer Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
entry.summary: South African human rights lawyer Navi Pillay wins the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her lifelong defense of human rights and international law.
